newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity down as generation units return.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity down as generation units return.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Monday as several western power generation units returned to service, industry sources said.
"It's being sold off in fairly light volume," said one New York based futures trader.

Weakness was seen from the return to service of the 1,080 megawatt (MW) San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS) unit 3 in southern California, which resumed electricity production Monday morning.
The adjacent 1,070 MW unit 2 was operating at 70 percent of capacity during maintenance work on a main feedwater pump.
Also, the 750 MW unit 2 at the Mohave coal-fired power plant in Nevada was restarted slightly ahead of schedule late Friday night, a plant spokesman said. The Mohave unit tripped off line a week ago.
Meanwhile, the 1,158 MW WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Richland, Washington, reached full power as of early Monday.
Several western coal-fired power plants were also scheduled to resume operation following outages, including the 254 MW Valmy unit 1 also in Nevada and a 700 MW unit at the Colstrip plant in Montana.

As of 1215 EDT, August Palo Verde (PV) was trading down $1.02 at $35.75 per megawatt hour (MWh) following trades in a range of $35.65-36.30, while September was down 61 cents at the day's low of $28.50 after trade as high as $28.70 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) was down 40 cents at the day's low of $21.50 after trade as high as $21.60, while September was down 39 cents at the day's high of $21.80 following trade as low as $21.70 per MWh.
NYMEX said as of 1135 an estimated total of 81 COB and 137 PV contracts had traded.
Six-to-ten day forecasts called for cooler than normal summer weather in the Northwest and along the California coast and seasonal temperatures in the interior section of the Southwest.
As of 1215 EDT, August Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 6.3 cents at $2.105 per million British thermal units.
